problem:
Let $z$ be a complex number such that $z^{13} = 1.$  Let $w_1,$ $w_2,$ $\dots,$ $w_k$ be all the possible values of
\[z + z^3 + z^4 + z^9 + z^{10} + z^{12}.\]Find $w_1^2 + w_2^2 + \dots + w_k^2.$
response_with_ans:
The solutions to $z^{13} = 1$ are the 13th roots of unity.  These are of the form
\[e^{2 \pi i k/13},\]where $0 \le k \le 12.$

Let
\[S = z + z^3 + z^4 + z^9 + z^{10} + z^{12}.\]Then
\begin{align*}
z^3 S &= z^4 + z^6 + z^7 + z^{12} + z^{13} + z^{15} \\
&= z^4 + z^6 + z^7 + z^{12} + 1 + z^2,
\end{align*}and
\begin{align*}
z^9 S &= z^{10} + z^{12} + z^{13} + z^{18} + z^{19} + z^{21} \\
&= z^{10} + z^{12} + 1 + z^5 + z^6 + z^8.
\end{align*}Hence,
\[(1 + z^3 + z^9) S = 1 + z^2 + z^4 + z^5 + z^6 + z^7 + z^8 + z^{10} + z^{12}.\]We can write this as
\[(1 + z^3 + z^9) S = \frac{z^{13} - 1}{z - 1} = 0.\]Since $z \neq 1,$ $1 + z^3 + z^9 = 0.$

Let $\omega = e^{2 \pi i/13}.$  Then
\[S = \omega + \omega^3 + \omega^4 + \omega^9 + \omega^{10} + \omega^{12}.\]Note that
\[\overline{S} = \omega^{-1} + \omega^{-3} + \omega^{-4} + \omega^{-9} + \omega^{-10} + \omega^{-12} = \omega^{12} + \omega^{10} + \omega^9 + \omega^4 + \omega^3 + \omega.\]Hence, $S = \overline{S},$ so $S$ is real.

Also,
\begin{align*}
S^2 &= (\omega + \omega^3 + \omega^4 + \omega^9 + \omega^{10} + \omega^{12})^2 \\
&= \omega^2 + \omega^6 + \omega^8 + \omega^{18} + \omega^{20} + \omega^{24} \\
&\quad + 2(\omega^4 + \omega^7 + \omega^8 + \omega^{13} + \omega^{14} + \omega^{16} + \omega^{17} + \omega^{19} + \omega^{21} + \omega^{22} + \omega^{23} + \omega^{25}) \\
&= \omega^2 + \omega^6 + \omega^8 + \omega^5 + \omega^7 + \omega^{11} \\
&\quad + 2(\omega^4 + \omega^7 + \omega^8 + \omega + \omega^2 + \omega^4 + \omega^5 + \omega^6 + \omega^8 + \omega^9 + \omega^{10} + \omega^{12}) \\
&= 3 + 2 \omega + 2 \omega^2 + 3 \omega^4 + 2 \omega^5 + 2 \omega^6 + 2 \omega^7 + 2 \omega^8 + 2 \omega^9 + 2 \omega^{10} + 2 \omega^{11} + 2 \omega^{12}.
\end{align*}Let
\[T = 3 + 2 \omega + 2 \omega^2 + 3 \omega^4 + 2 \omega^5 + 2 \omega^6 + 2 \omega^7 + 2 \omega^8 + 2 \omega^9 + 2 \omega^{10} + 2 \omega^{11} + 2 \omega^{12}.\]Then
\begin{align*}
\omega^3 T &= 3 \omega^3 + 2 \omega^4 + 2 \omega^5 + 3 \omega^7 + 2 \omega^8 + 2 \omega^9 + 2 \omega^{10} + 2 \omega^{11} + 2 \omega^{12} + 2 \omega^{13} + 2 \omega^{14} + 2 \omega^{15} \\
&= 3 \omega^3 + 2 \omega^4 + 2 \omega^5 + 3 \omega^7 + 2 \omega^8 + 2 \omega^9 + 2 \omega^{10} + 2 \omega^{11} + 2 \omega^{12} + 2 + 2 \omega + 2 \omega^2,
\end{align*}and
\begin{align*}
\omega^9 T &= 3 \omega^9 + 2 \omega^{10} + 2 \omega^{11} + 3 \omega^{13} + 2 \omega^{14} + 2 \omega^{15} + 2 \omega^{16} + 2 \omega^{17} + 2 \omega^{18} + 2 \omega^{19} + 2 \omega^{20} + 2 \omega^{21} \\
&= 3 \omega^9 + 2 \omega^{10} + 2 \omega^{11} + 3 + 2 \omega + 2 \omega^2 + 2 \omega^3 + 2 \omega^4 + 2 \omega^5 + 2 \omega^6 + 2 \omega^7 + 2 \omega^8.
\end{align*}Hence,
\[(1 + \omega^3 + \omega^9) T = 6 + 4 \omega + 4 \omega^2 + 6 \omega^3 + 4 \omega^4 + 4 \omega^5 + 4 \omega^6 + 4 \omega^7 + 4 \omega^8 + 4 \omega^9 + 4 \omega^{10} + 4 \omega^{11} + 4 \omega^{12}.\]Since $1 + \omega^3 + \omega^9 = 0,$
\[6 + 4 \omega + 4 \omega^2 + 6 \omega^3 + 4 \omega^4 + 4 \omega^5 + 4 \omega^6 + 4 \omega^7 + 4 \omega^8 + 4 \omega^9 + 4 \omega^{10} + 4 \omega^{11} + 4 \omega^{12} = 0.\]Then
\[4 \omega + 4 \omega^2 + 4 \omega^3 + 4 \omega^4 + 4 \omega^5 + 4 \omega^6 + 4 \omega^7 + 4 \omega^8 + 4 \omega^9 + 4 \omega^{10} + 4 \omega^{11} + 4 \omega^{12} = -6.\]Hence, $T = 3 - \frac{3}{2} = \frac{3}{2}.$

Thus, $S^2 = \frac{3}{2},$ so $S = \pm \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}.$  Since $S$ is real, $S = \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}$ or $S = -\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}.$

If $S = \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}},$ then the 13th roots of unity that satisfy this equation are the roots of
\[z^{12} + z^{10} + z^9 + z^4 + z^3 + z - \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} = 0.\]If $S = -\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}},$ then the 13th roots of unity that satisfy this equation are the roots of
\[z^{12} + z^{10} + z^9 + z^4 + z^3 + z + \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} = 0.\]Let $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $\dots,$ $a_6$ be the roots of the first equation, and let $b_1,$ $b_2,$ $\dots,$ $b_6$ be the roots of the second equation.  Then
\begin{align*}
a_1^2 + a_2^2 + \dots + a_6^2 &= (a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_6)^2 - 2(a_1 a_2 + a_1 a_3 + \dots + a_5 a_6) \\
&= 0^2 - 2 \cdot -\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \\
&= \sqrt{6},
\end{align*}and
\begin{align*}
b_1^2 + b_2^2 + \dots + b_6^2 &= (b_1 + b_2 + \dots + b_6)^2 - 2(b_1 b_2 + b_1 b_3 + \dots + b_5 b_6) \\
&= 0^2 - 2 \cdot \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \\
&= -\sqrt{6}.
\end{align*}Hence, $w_1^2 + w_2^2 + \dots + w_k^2 = \boxed{0}.$
